video_title: Jeff Yan's Plan to Bring the Entire Financial Industry Onto Hyperliquid | Odd Lots
gist: Hyperliquid Labs CEO Jeff Yan explains Hyperliquid as a neutral on-chain layer aiming to 'house all of finance', detailing HIP-3 permissionless deployers (500,000 HYPE stake, 31-hour Dutch auctions), oracle rules (1% clamp), and on-chain clearing. He argues perps can lead price discovery over thin underlyings, incumbents will become deployers like AWS adopters, and regulators may oversee deployers rather than the protocol as the CFTC weighs US access.

themes.theme: Hyperliquid vision: neutral layer to house all finance

insights.claim: Jeff Yan describes Hyperliquid as a protocol whose aspirational goal is to 'house all of finance', a neutral layer that is a step-function improvement over electronic but fragmented markets, analogous to electronic trading's leap over pit trading.
insights.speaker: Jeff Yan (co-founder & CEO, Hyperliquid Labs)
insights.so_what: The pitch is market-structure consolidation onto one global ledger, not just another crypto venue.
insights.quote: We view Hyperliquid, the protocol as a sort of step function improvement over electronic but fragmented markets.

insights.claim: Yan says capturing even 90% of all finance would be a huge success, but concedes Hyperliquid is a long way from that goal.
insights.speaker: Jeff Yan (co-founder & CEO, Hyperliquid Labs)
insights.so_what: Ambition is total-market scale; current share is small, so the thesis is long-dated optionality.
insights.quote: I think even 90% of all of finance would be a huge success. And we're a long way ways away.

insights.claim: Yan claims no other blockchain besides Hyperliquid has the precise vision of a global financial system running on one single global state.
insights.speaker: Jeff Yan (co-founder & CEO, Hyperliquid Labs)
insights.so_what: Differentiation vs general-purpose chains rests on a finance-specific single-state design.
insights.quote: I don't think any of them, other than Hyperliquid, you know, has this precise vision of a global financial system can actually just have one global state.

insights.claim: Yan insists Hyperliquid is not trying to displace incumbents; whether markets are perpetuals or dated futures is irrelevant because what matters is an order book, a clearing system, global distribution and concentration of liquidity.
insights.speaker: Jeff Yan (co-founder & CEO, Hyperliquid Labs)
insights.so_what: Positions Hyperliquid as infrastructure vendor to incumbents rather than competitor, easing adoption and regulatory friction.
insights.quote: Like we are not we're not trying to displace anything.

insights.claim: The founding thesis in 2023 was that centralized crypto venues offering perpetual futures had clear product-market fit, and the opportunity was to combine centralized-exchange UX with on-chain self-custody to remove exchange counterparty risk.
insights.speaker: Jeff Yan (co-founder & CEO, Hyperliquid Labs)
insights.so_what: Hyperliquid's growth thesis is self-custodied perps with CEX-grade UX; counterparty-risk events at centralized venues favor it.
insights.quote: I think the the kind of counterparty risk of using exchange is always going to be there, whether it's in a crypto or non crypto context.

insights.claim: Hyperliquid did not raise VC money, and Yan (formerly at Hudson River Trading) found that no existing chain could house all of finance with incremental improvements, forcing the team to rebuild down to the consensus layer.
insights.speaker: Jeff Yan (co-founder & CEO, Hyperliquid Labs)
insights.so_what: Vertical, ground-up build explains performance claims and a lean, founder-controlled cap structure.

themes.theme: Protocol mechanics: HIP-3 deployers, oracles, auctions

insights.claim: Under Hyperliquid's permissionless deployment system (HIP-3), a deployer must stake 500,000 HYPE tokens (not $500,000 worth) to unlock the ability to deploy markets, inheriting the protocol's order book, clearing and USDC integration.
insights.speaker: Jeff Yan (co-founder & CEO, Hyperliquid Labs)
insights.so_what: Deployer staking creates structural demand/lockup for HYPE that scales with the number of markets.
insights.quote: they have to stake 500,000 currently.

insights.claim: Deployment slots are scarce because each order book and clearing system consumes network compute, and they are allocated by an on-chain Dutch auction run every 31 hours (chosen because 31 is relatively prime to 24 so the reset rotates across time zones).
insights.speaker: Jeff Yan (co-founder & CEO, Hyperliquid Labs)
insights.so_what: Slot scarcity plus auction pricing gives deployment rights an observable market value tied to demand for new markets.
insights.quote: in every 31 hour interval, currently 31 is simply chosen so that the the time at which the auction resets, is the changes, time zones, as it's relatively prime to the number 24.

insights.claim: The Dutch auction price decreases linearly from a starting value, the first bidder wins, and the starting price resets to twice the last clearing price, creating a self-correcting approach to fair value that avoids sniping and penny-bidding games of normal auctions.
insights.speaker: Jeff Yan (co-founder & CEO, Hyperliquid Labs)
insights.so_what: Auction clearing prices are a transparent on-chain signal of demand for new listings.
insights.quote: it resets to twice the last clearing price.

insights.claim: Yan expects deployment resources to become less scarce as the network scales, but says compute will always be some limiting factor for deployers.
insights.speaker: Jeff Yan (co-founder & CEO, Hyperliquid Labs)
insights.so_what: Slot prices may fall over time with scaling, diluting the value of early deployment rights.

insights.claim: A perpetual contract ultimately reduces to one exogenous number, the oracle index price, which the deployer defines and publishes; Yan predicts that as spot markets move onto Hyperliquid, oracles could be derived on-chain rather than published externally.
insights.speaker: Jeff Yan (co-founder & CEO, Hyperliquid Labs)
insights.so_what: On-chain spot liquidity would reduce oracle-manipulation and off-chain dependency risk.
insights.quote: as spot markets move on to Hyperliquid, you can imagine a system where the Oracle is actually no longer published, but rather derived from ongoing problems.

insights.claim: The protocol enforces a hard rule that consecutive oracle price updates cannot differ by more than 1%; a push 2% away is clamped to 1%, breaking big jumps into near-continuous moves so liquidations proceed orderly.
insights.speaker: Jeff Yan (co-founder & CEO, Hyperliquid Labs)
insights.so_what: Gap risk is smoothed mechanically, which matters for leveraged traders around weekend/news gaps.
insights.quote: between two oracle price updates, the relative difference between those two prices cannot be more than 1%.

insights.claim: The protocol makes no subjective liquidity judgments about whether a deployed market makes sense; like an order-book software vendor, it only enforces mathematical constraints.
insights.speaker: Jeff Yan (co-founder & CEO, Hyperliquid Labs)
insights.so_what: Market-quality risk sits with deployers and traders, not the protocol; due diligence must be per-deployer.
insights.quote: We can't do subjective liquidity, judgments.

insights.claim: Liquidation and the default-waterfall analog are rules-based and executed autonomously by HyperCore, the on-chain clearing submodule, rather than by anyone setting liquidation prices.
insights.speaker: Jeff Yan (co-founder & CEO, Hyperliquid Labs)
insights.so_what: Transparent deterministic clearing is the core differentiation vs opaque centralized risk engines.

insights.claim: Consensus assumes two-thirds of stake is non-Byzantine; about 30-something validators exist and the top 27 by stake operate the network at any time, on modest hardware requiring about 128GB of RAM.
insights.speaker: Jeff Yan (co-founder & CEO, Hyperliquid Labs)
insights.so_what: Low node requirements support decentralization claims, though a 27-validator active set is still concentrated.
insights.quote: right now, you need 128 gigs of Ram.

insights.claim: Joe Weisenthal notes the auction process means Hyperliquid lacks the thousands of spam 'dog coins' found on Solana or Ethereum, since the protocol itself sets exchange listing rules.
insights.speaker: Joe Weisenthal (host)
insights.so_what: Curated-by-price listings make Hyperliquid look more like a governed exchange than an open chain.

themes.theme: Derivatives over the underlying: price discovery and funding

insights.claim: Tracy Alloway's 'inverse pyramid' thesis: as in media, the underlying asset is now the smallest layer of markets, with derivatives, leveraged ETFs, tokenized versions and prediction markets stacking ever larger on top.
insights.speaker: Tracy Alloway (host)
insights.so_what: Expect continued growth of derivative wrappers relative to cash markets, benefiting venues that host them.
insights.quote: the underlying is kind of the smallest part of the market now, and there are so many new instruments built on top of it

insights.claim: Yan argues perp volume need not be capped relative to underlying volume, citing index futures and ETFs vs their components: what matters is that liquidity providers stand ready to trade against mispricings, so price discovery can happen on the derivative.
insights.speaker: Jeff Yan (co-founder & CEO, Hyperliquid Labs)
insights.so_what: Thin underlying markets don't by themselves invalidate high-volume perps, rebutting a common manipulation critique.
insights.quote: And so you get this effect where the price discovery can happen on a derivative.

insights.claim: Weisenthal raises the Mango Markets incident on Solana, where trading size relative to a thin underlying token allowed manipulation transmitted through the oracle, as the key risk for oracle-based perps.
insights.speaker: Joe Weisenthal (host)
insights.so_what: Oracle manipulation on illiquid underlyings remains the main tail risk for permissionless perp listings.

insights.claim: Yan says perps do not need a 24/7 underlying oracle: funding can alternate between periods of free-floating derivative price and periods of funding payments based on the discrepancy, still converging, just more slowly.
insights.speaker: Jeff Yan (co-founder & CEO, Hyperliquid Labs)
insights.so_what: Explains how weekend WTI/Brent perps can trade with no live spot market, and why weekend prices may drift from Monday opens.
insights.quote: You could actually have funding.

insights.claim: Hyperliquid drew attention this spring after the war in Iran broke out because it offered 24/7 WTI and Brent perp trading when traditional markets were closed.
insights.speaker: Joe Weisenthal (host)
insights.so_what: Geopolitical weekend shocks are a demand catalyst for 24/7 commodity perps.
insights.quote: here is a venue that had 24 or 7 WTI, WTI and Brant futures trading at it.

insights.claim: Weisenthal says the perp 'primitive' and 24/7 trading both feel inevitable regardless of Hyperliquid's own fate.
insights.speaker: Joe Weisenthal (host)
insights.so_what: Structural tailwind for perp venues and 24/7 market infrastructure broadly.
insights.quote: It feels very inevitable, as does 24 seven trading at this point.

insights.claim: Bloomberg now has a Hyperliquid (HYPE) page showing 24/7 trading in Brent, WTI, S&P 500, Circle, SanDisk and Micron perps; Weisenthal sees terminal listing, as with Bitcoin around 2012-2013, as a sign something is becoming a big deal.
insights.speaker: Joe Weisenthal (host)
insights.so_what: Mainstream data integration signals institutional attention to on-chain equity/commodity perps.

insights.claim: Deployer trade.xyz's SK Hynix market that suffered a bad quote earlier this year, causing the oracle price to deviate dramatically and losses; Yan calls it an implementation issue, with a postmortem and refunds issued.
insights.speaker: Jeff Yan (co-founder & CEO, Hyperliquid Labs)
insights.so_what: Deployer-level oracle errors are a real operational risk for HIP-3 equity perps.
insights.quote: that falls in the category of implementation issue.

insights.claim: Yan argues that with trillion-dollar IPOs, most wealth creation has already happened by listing, and the gating of pre-IPO exposure to few people is a failing of the current system that permissionless perps can address.
insights.speaker: Jeff Yan (co-founder & CEO, Hyperliquid Labs)
insights.so_what: Pre-IPO perps (e.g., on private AI companies) are a likely growth vector for HIP-3 deployers.
insights.quote: if you have trillion dollar, 2 trillion, $3 trillion companies IPO, there's you can pretty confidently say that most of the wealth creation has happened at that point.

insights.claim: Alloway counters that a perp tracking a company like Anthropic gives no claim on cash flows or dividends; Yan concedes it is not a strict improvement but notes futures don't confer cash flows either, and frames suitability as an education problem.
insights.speaker: Jeff Yan (co-founder & CEO, Hyperliquid Labs)
insights.so_what: Tracking perps are synthetic price exposure, not ownership, a key risk-disclosure point for regulators.
insights.quote: I'm not saying that it's a strict improvement over the system.

insights.claim: Yan says many of the larger traders on Hyperliquid are institutions, since market making requires significant sophistication.
insights.speaker: Jeff Yan (co-founder & CEO, Hyperliquid Labs)
insights.so_what: Liquidity on the venue is substantially institutionally provided.
insights.quote: I think many of the larger, larger traders are institutions.

insights.claim: US users are currently barred by the terms of service of interfaces from trading derivatives on Hyperliquid, but the CFTC and the current administration (Trump mentioned Hyperliquid) want a proactive approach to bringing on-chain finance rails to the US.
insights.speaker: Jeff Yan (co-founder & CEO, Hyperliquid Labs)
insights.so_what: Potential US opening is a major addressable-market catalyst for Hyperliquid and HYPE.

insights.claim: Yan agrees regulators could plausibly regulate deployers rather than the protocol, analogous to TCP/IP being unregulated while the layers with controls are regulated.
insights.speaker: Jeff Yan (co-founder & CEO, Hyperliquid Labs)
insights.so_what: A deployer-regulated model would let registered entities (e.g., exchanges) list on Hyperliquid without the protocol itself registering.
insights.quote: Right? The regulation sits at the, at the layer where there are controls.

insights.claim: Yan argues on-chain markets turn proof of reserves from a process into a property: anyone can provably audit that the sum of user balances equals the USDC at an address.
insights.speaker: Jeff Yan (co-founder & CEO, Hyperliquid Labs)
insights.so_what: Continuous verifiable solvency is the strongest regulatory selling point vs traditional attest-on-request models.
insights.quote: Whereas if this is a property rather than a process, all of a sudden, I think I just think this kind of like moment is, is quite, it's quite beneficial.

insights.claim: Yan says regulators are conservative and slower to see the benefits, with the gap being whether the technology is compatible with CFTC core principles, which are technology-agnostic.
insights.speaker: Jeff Yan (co-founder & CEO, Hyperliquid Labs)
insights.so_what: US access is likely gradual; timeline risk remains despite political support.

insights.claim: Yan rejects calling banks and asset managers 'legacy', predicting they will adopt Hyperliquid as infrastructure like companies adopted AWS cloud, and could eventually become deployers.
insights.speaker: Jeff Yan (co-founder & CEO, Hyperliquid Labs)
insights.so_what: Institutional deployers would expand listings and legitimacy; watch for bank/exchange HIP-3 announcements.
insights.quote: There's a bit of like the analogy here with the cloud, you know, in AWS.

insights.claim: Yan mentions a Kraken announcement and says a Nasdaq-traded digital asset treasury company is part of the broader ecosystem pitching the technology to investors, framing 'who runs Hyperliquid' as a constellation of teams.
insights.speaker: Jeff Yan (co-founder & CEO, Hyperliquid Labs)
insights.so_what: Ecosystem includes listed vehicles and major exchanges, offering public-market exposure routes.

insights.claim: Hosts flag an under-explored metagame: deployers must pick which new markets (e.g., hypothetical Central Asian/Kazakhstan index perps) will attract volume before bidding in the auction.
insights.speaker: Joe Weisenthal (host)
insights.so_what: Deployer economics hinge on picking listings ahead of demand; auction data reveals where they think demand is heading.
